emergency.condition_text: a sweeper is coming, or is on the stack, and your board is committed
indications: A seat has four or more untapped lands, has cast nothing this turn cycle, and passed with the mana up.
Somebody has named you the problem out loud. Log 001, turn three: five Vampires for three mana spent, 'this is ridiculous', and every answer at the table pointed at Edgar from then on.
You have more bodies on the battlefield than the other seats combined.
No death payoff is on the battlefield: no Blood Artist, no Cruel Celebrant, no Cordial Vampire, no Elenda, the Dusk Rose, no Crossway Troublemakers, no Skullclamp, no Liliana, Dreadhorde General.
Anointed Procession, Caretaker's Talent or Sanguine Bond is on the battlefield. Those are enchantments, and Flawless Maneuver and Akroma's Will name creatures.
Two of the five logged games are filed under a sweeper, and the deck has no sweeper of its own by role.
immediate: Count the untapped lands at every seat before you cast your next Vampire, and name the seat that can sweep.
Put a death payoff on the battlefield ahead of any further body. Cast Cruel Celebrant before Blood Artist: Celebrant bills each opponent, Blood Artist bills one target player.
Stop deploying at the body that beats the table's board. Keep the next Vampire and the next doubler in hand.

With a death payoff on the battlefield and the sweeper on the stack, sacrifice Elenda, the Dusk Rose to a free outlet, then let the sweeper resolve. She leaves 1/1 lifelink Vampires equal to her power, and each of them dies to the sweeper and bills the table again.

Spend Boros Charm or Teferi's Protection only on the enchantments. Those two are the cards in the 99 that save Anointed Procession, Caretaker's Talent and Sanguine Bond; Flawless Maneuver and Akroma's Will leave them to die.
subsequent: Cast a Vampire at mana value two or less to restart eminence. Thirteen are declared in the 99 and one is in hand in 95.0% of goldfish games, mean turn 2.22.
Take Crossway Troublemakers' draw one trigger at a time and decline the 2 life on every trigger past the cards you need.
Redeploy the worst threat first and keep the best one in hand for the second sweeper.
Rebuild to the payoff, not to the bodies: a free outlet and a drain beat five 1/1 tokens.
Cast Edgar Markov the first turn you can pay six. In log 001 he arrived at eight mana, and the turn he landed took a seat to 1 life.
emergency.notes: Teferi's Protection phases your board out, so nothing dies and no death payoff fires. On a board holding Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant, Elenda, the Dusk Rose, Crossway Troublemakers or Skullclamp it turns the refuel off. Log 002 prices the other choice: a wipe with the drains online killed eleven creatures, took 11 life off every opponent, gained 11, and left the pilot at 50 against a table at 20. Cast Teferi's Protection to save an engine you cannot rebuild, not creatures you can.

emergency.condition_text: one seat is answering your permanents one at a time
indications: The same seat has answered a permanent of yours on two consecutive turns. Log 002: Anointed Procession resolved and was removed the following turn, and the card-flow permanents went the same way.
An opponent is pinging your 1/1 tokens instead of attacking your large bodies. Log 004: Tom's Goblin Sharpshooter did this all game and fed the draw.
Your own answers have been in hand for two turns. Goldfish holds interaction in 88.3% of games by turn six and can pay for it in 26.9%.
Your mana is fully spent on bodies every turn. Log 002 names that as the structural half: a deck that cannot afford to hold up interaction does not run interaction.
The permanent they answered was a doubler or a draw engine, not a body.
immediate: Name the seat answering you and count its untapped mana.

Leave one answer's worth of mana unspent from this turn on. Despark costs two, Anguished Unmaking and Stroke of Midnight three, Path to Exile one; Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver cost nothing while Edgar Markov is on the battlefield.
Spend that answer on the permanent that is answering you, not on the largest board.
Equip Skullclamp to a 1/1 eminence token for {1} and draw two. Their next removal spell then costs them a card and costs you nothing.
Redeploy in this order: free outlet, death payoff, doubler. The doubler draws the answer, so it goes last.
subsequent: Re-equip Blade of the Bloodchief for {1} on your turn after they kill the body carrying it. The Equipment survives creature removal; the counters on the body do not.
Cast the doubler on a turn you also cast a Vampire, so the extra bodies arrive before the answer does.
Deploy the bodies that pay when they die first: Elenda, the Dusk Rose, Bloodtracker, Crossway Troublemakers, Liliana, Dreadhorde General.
Recount the answering seat's mana each turn and cast into the window where it is tapped out.
emergency.notes: Read High-Society Hunter's clause before you count on it as a death payoff: it sees another NONTOKEN creature dying, so it is blind to every eminence token. Two further limits belong on the same page: Deflecting Swat only redirects a spell or ability that targets, and nothing in the 99 answers a land. No logged game is filed under this cause; logs 002 and 004 describe it from inside two games filed elsewhere.

emergency.condition_text: an opponent is assembling a two-card kill and you hold no counterspell
indications: A seat has tutored. Log 004: Tom tutored a two-card infinite and closed the game before the pilot's lethal attack resolved.
A seat has stopped developing and holds no creatures. That is the seat that killed the table in log 004.
A seat is holding up mana and passing every turn.
There are no counterspells in the 99. Once a piece resolves, the answers are Despark, Anguished Unmaking and Stroke of Midnight, or nothing.
immediate: Name the seat that has stopped developing.
Attack that seat first, ahead of the seat with the biggest board.
Cast Despark or Anguished Unmaking on a combo piece the turn it resolves. Both are instants, and the piece's resolution is the last profitable moment.
If the kill spell or ability targets, cast Deflecting Swat and change the target.

Cast Vampiric Tutor in the end step before your turn for the missing half of your own route: Bloodletter of Aclazotz if Sanctum Seeker is out (stack 003), or Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or Sanguine Bond if Bloodthirsty Conqueror is out (stacks 004 and 006). It puts the card on top, so your draw step is what finds it.
subsequent: Take the drain window the turn it opens. Both verified loops end a pod turn on their own and need no combat damage; the attack does not.
Count every opponent's untapped mana before you declare lethal.
Recast Edgar Markov and rebuild the outlet-and-payoff pair. Eminence mints from a zone no answer reaches.
emergency.notes: The infinite is the ceiling, not the plan, and the pilot's stated direction keeps it subordinate rather than cutting it. Bloodthirsty Conqueror with Vito or Sanguine Bond assembles in 7.8% of goldfish games (15.1% with Vampiric Tutor) and 3.4% by turn six; the Bloodletter route assembles in 4.1% (9.4% assisted) and 1.6% by turn six. Both rest on one body each. Play the drain engine underneath them. Log 004's board was winning when the combo landed.

emergency.condition_text: the board is even, you have cast one Vampire this game, and your hand does nothing
indications: You have cast one Vampire this game and Edgar Markov is already on the battlefield. Log 003 is that game exactly, from a turn-one four-mana opener.
Every opponent has a blocker larger than your largest Vampire.
No draw engine is on the battlefield. Goldfish draws one in 83.5% of games at mean turn 2.62, so this is the other 16.5%.
Your hand is lands.
'Ran out of steam' or 'no card draw' is the cause the pilot names in logs 001, 002 and 003.
immediate: Cast Reactor Raid for {2}{B}: sacrifice a token or an artifact, draw two, and play Midgar, City of Mako from exile on a later turn.
Equip Skullclamp to a 1/1 eminence token for {1} and draw two.
Cast the draw body before the lord: Bloodtracker, Champion of Dusk, Welcoming Vampire, Preacher of the Schism, Crossway Troublemakers.
Pay {B} and 2 life to Bloodtracker on every turn it is on the battlefield. It draws one card per +1/+1 counter when it leaves. Log 004 names skipping this as the missed line of the night.
Attack with Crossway Troublemakers on the battlefield. Attacking Vampires have deathtouch and lifelink, so a stalled board trades up.
subsequent: Equip Blade of the Bloodchief to a lifelink Vampire for {1} and sacrifice tokens to a free outlet. Each death puts two counters on the equipped body, which is how a stalled board produces one Vampire worth attacking with.
Activate Castle Locthwain for {1}{B}{B} while your hand is empty. It bills life equal to your hand size, which is why it is cheapest here.
Channel Takenuma, Abandoned Mire for {3}{B}, one less per legendary creature you control, to mill three and return a creature.
Cast Night's Whisper for two cards and 2 life, and stop paying life once a drain seat is live.
emergency.notes: The 28 August pivot asked for a self-mill package as a second way to dig and it was never built. Altar of Dementia and Takenuma, Abandoned Mire are the only cards in the 99 that mill, and Takenuma is the only one that returns anything from your graveyard. Until that changes the dig is card draw and the eminence tokens that feed it, so the outlet goes down before the lord, every time.

emergency.condition_text: the table has agreed you are the archenemy and is pointing its answers at you
indications: Somebody said it out loud on turn three. Log 001: five Vampires for three mana spent, 'this is ridiculous', and every answer at the table pointed at Edgar from then on.
You are the highest-life seat. Lifelink bodies, Elenda, the Dusk Rose and Preacher of the Schism push you there fast; log 002 had you at 50 against a table at 20 with an empty hand.
Two seats have passed with mana up while a third develops.
Your board shows a doubler. Anointed Procession, Mondrak, Glory Dominus and Elspeth, Storm Slayer are what a table reads as the threat.
immediate: Deploy the free outlet and the death drain before the doubler. Tokens and lifelink bodies read as fair.
Keep Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Bloodletter of Aclazotz and Sanctum Seeker in hand until the turn you use them. In log 001 both cards that would have refuelled the deck were countered on the way down.
Point Blood Artist's drain at the seat the table has already agreed to kill.
Attack the seat that is winning and give the reason as board position. Log 004 removed Alex first on exactly that ground.
Spend your removal on the permanent that is answering you and leave the biggest board for somebody else to handle.
subsequent: Rebuild after each wipe. The low curve put a real board back in one or two turns, three times, in log 001.
Recount who has the most life each turn. Preacher of the Schism draws while you are highest and mints a lifelink token while you attack the highest.
Take the drain window the turn it opens, and expect every held answer to appear the moment you present lethal.
emergency.notes: The only measurement the bench holds on who gets attacked is Forge's AI, and its own limits file says it is not human politics: no deals, no grudges, no table talk, no memory of last turn. It attacks the seat that has dealt the most combat damage 69.2% of the time, 95% interval [0.682, 0.702], across 7,949 decisions in 840 games. Read it as a claim about how a board LOOKS, not about your pod. No logged game is filed under this cause; log 001 describes the dynamic and is filed under a sweeper.

emergency.condition_text: a seat is killing you with damage you cannot block, and your drain has not closed the table
indications: A seat is dealing damage without attacking. Log 005: Tom's Purphoros pings finished the game while your board was the largest at the table and Oliver was a turn behind all night.
A planeswalker is on the battlefield and no untapped Vampire is at home. Log 005: Elspeth was exposed while the attack went all-in on Tom, and she was taken down before the pings finished you.
You are the lowest-life seat and still paying for lands and cards.
The seat racing you has flyers and your Vampires are on the ground.
Against a pod holding a Purphoros pinger model, Forge eliminated this seat in 35 of 40 games, 12 of them by that seat, all 21 recorded eliminations by damage (n40, 2026-09-03, on v1.1.0).
immediate: Name the seat that is faster and count the damage it deals per permanent it plays, not the power on its board.

Keep one deathtouch body home before you attack: Gifted Aetherborn, Vampire of the Dire Moon, Nighthawk Scavenger, Vampire Cutthroat. If Edgar Markov is on the battlefield, hold Deflecting Swat instead and attack with everything.

Spend Anguished Unmaking or Despark on the damage source. Those two are the interaction copies that exile a noncreature permanent; Stroke of Midnight destroys, and Path to Exile, Winds of Abandon, Elspeth's -3 and Vish Kal want a creature.

Stop paying life. Skip Champion of Dusk, Night's Whisper, Castle Locthwain, Bloodtracker's activation, Crossway Troublemakers' 2 life and Vampiric Tutor until the race is decided. A full tap cycle of this manabase costs 8 life.
Cast Teferi's Protection on the turn the table can kill you. Until your next turn your life total cannot change, and it is the one card in the 99 whose text stops life loss.
subsequent: Declare lethal the turn it is on the board. Logs 004 and 005 both reached a dominant board and lost after it.
Resolve Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or Sanguine Bond before the lifelink attack, so every point you gain is a point an opponent loses.
Attack with every Vampire while Sanctum Seeker is on the battlefield. Each attacking Vampire bills each opponent for 1 whether or not it connects.
Cast Akroma's Will with Edgar Markov on the battlefield and choose both modes: flying, vigilance and double strike, plus lifelink, indestructible and protection from each colour.
Recount your life against the table's before you pay for another card.
emergency.notes: Path to Exile and an overloaded Winds of Abandon hand the seat you slowed a basic land, and nothing in the 99 answers a land, so both leave a racing seat with more mana than it started with. Two limits on the figures: Forge's runs read the combat half only, because life loss that is not damage, which is every drain in this deck, never appears in a damage figure; and the Purphoros run above was measured on v1.1.0, one version behind the list you are holding.

emergency.condition_text: you are short of black or short of a land drop, and the board has stalled at two bodies
indications: Black is the short colour: 32 sources against a 36 target, 78.5% on curve on lands alone and 85.5% with the rocks, across 38 black cards and 54 black pips.
You are holding Bloodletter of Aclazotz. Its {1}{B}{B}{B} is the only cost in the 99 with three identical coloured pips.
You missed a land drop. Goldfish hits turn three in 91.9% of games and turn six in 59.8%.
Your untapped lands are the ones that bill you: City of Brass, Mana Confluence, Caves of Koilos, Sulfurous Springs, Battlefield Forge, Silent Clearing and Ancient Tomb.
Three lands enter tapped unconditionally (Midgar, City of Mako, Nomad Outpost, Savai Triome) and twelve more enter tapped off curve.
immediate: Play the land that makes black.
Cast the rock before the second body: Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Talisman of Indulgence, Herald's Horn or Patchwork Banner. One is in hand in 67.5% of games at mean turn 3.58.
Tap an untapped creature to Survivors' Encampment for the colour you are missing.
Sacrifice a creature to Master of Dark Rites for {B}{B}{B} and spend it on a Vampire, Cleric or Demon spell. That mana cannot pay an activated ability.
Stop tapping the painlands once you are the lowest-life seat. A full tap cycle of this manabase costs 8 life.
subsequent: Name Vampire on Herald's Horn as it enters and take the free look at the top card each upkeep.
Cast Night's Whisper or Champion of Dusk to find land, and stop paying life once a drain seat is live.
Crack Bloodstained Mire or Marsh Flats for the land that makes the colour you are missing, and take an untapped one where there is a choice.
Hold the doubler until you can cast it and a Vampire in the same turn.
emergency.notes: Nothing in the 99 answers a land: Despark, Anguished Unmaking and Stroke of Midnight are nonland-only, and Path to Exile and Winds of Abandon hit creatures. A land-based lock is raced, not answered. No logged game is filed under this cause, so this page is built from mana_analysis and the goldfish rather than from the table, and the pilot logs a missed land drop rather than a missed pip.

keep: A black source among the lands. Black carries 54 of the pips on 32 sources against a 36 target, and the model's keep rule counts lands and never their colours.
Two or three lands, or two lands plus Sol Ring, Arcane Signet or Talisman of Indulgence.

One play at mana value two or less: a Vampire, a free sacrifice outlet (Viscera Seer, Ashnod's Altar, Altar of Dementia), or a rock. Log 005 opened on a swamp into a turn-one Viscera Seer and held momentum all game.
A second spell you can cast by turn four: a draw engine (Bloodtracker, Welcoming Vampire, Preacher of the Schism, Skullclamp, Night's Whisper) or a second Vampire.
ship: Two lands with no black source and nothing at mana value one or two.
A hand whose only action is Edgar Markov.
Five or more lands with no Vampire at mana value two or less.
Answers and no bodies. There are no counterspells here and every drain needs creatures.
preflight.note: Read the colours by hand. The model's keep rule counts lands, so a two-land hand with no black source passes it and loses the game; log 002 kept that hand knowing better and names the keep as the mistake. On the model's own rule the deck can act by turn three in 96.4% of games at a mean 0.23 mulligans.

steps: Play the land that makes black.
Cast the rock before the second body: Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Talisman of Indulgence.
Cast a Vampire at mana value one or two every turn you can. Each mints a 1/1 from the command zone whether or not Edgar has been cast (stacks 002 and 010).
Name Vampire on Herald's Horn or Patchwork Banner as it enters.
Count the table's untapped mana at the end of turn three before you add a fourth body.
Put a free sacrifice outlet on the battlefield: Viscera Seer, Ashnod's Altar or Altar of Dementia. One is in hand in 72.3% of games at mean turn 3.16.
Put a death payoff beside it. Cruel Celebrant bills each opponent, Blood Artist bills one target player, Cordial Vampire puts a +1/+1 counter on every Vampire you control each time a creature dies.
Cast Edgar Markov the first turn you can pay six, and cast him before you commit a planeswalker. Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver cost nothing only while he is on the battlefield.
Cast the doubler after the outlet and the payoff, not before.
Equip Skullclamp to a 1/1 eminence token and draw two, or equip Blade of the Bloodchief to a lifelink Vampire and feed the outlet.
Sacrifice a token to the free outlet every turn a death payoff is on the battlefield.
Draw before you deploy: Reactor Raid, Skullclamp, Bloodtracker, Castle Locthwain, Minas Tirith.
Pay {B} and 2 life to Bloodtracker on every turn it is on the battlefield.
Attack the seat with the most life with Preacher of the Schism for a 1/1 lifelink Vampire, and draw a card off it on every turn you are the seat with the most life.
Leave one answer's worth of mana unspent. Goldfish holds interaction in 88.3% of games by turn six and can pay for it in 26.9%.
Count the damage on the board before anything else: board power, plus 1 per attacking Vampire per opponent from Sanctum Seeker, plus 1 per opponent per death from Cruel Celebrant.

Name the route if the board is short: Sanctum Seeker attacking with Bloodletter of Aclazotz out (stack 003), or Bloodthirsty Conqueror with Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or Sanguine Bond (stacks 004 and 006).
Count every opponent's untapped mana and name the answer each seat can be holding.
Hold Deflecting Swat or Flawless Maneuver up for the turn you commit, not the turn after. Both are free while Edgar Markov is on the battlefield.
Declare the attack the turn lethal is on the board. Logs 004 and 005 both reached a dominant board and lost after it.

optics: A board of 1/1 tokens and lifelink bodies reads as fair. Anointed Procession, Mondrak, Glory Dominus and Elspeth, Storm Slayer are what a table reads as the threat, so they land after the outlet and the payoff.
Five bodies on turn three off three mana spent is what got this deck named archenemy in log 001. Price the attention in rather than trying to avoid it.
Lifelink, Elenda, the Dusk Rose and Preacher of the Schism make you the visible leader while your hand empties. Log 002: 50 life against a table at 20, with nothing left to cast.

Forge's AI attacks the seat that has dealt the most combat damage 69.2% of the time, [0.682, 0.702] over 7,949 decisions. Its own limits file records no deals, no grudges and no memory, so take it as a reading on how a board looks, not on your pod.
reveal: Show the tokens. Keep Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Bloodletter of Aclazotz and Sanguine Bond in hand until the turn they close: log 001 lost Bloodthirsty Conqueror to a counterspell on the way down.
Cast the doubler on a turn you also cast a Vampire, so the extra bodies arrive before the answer does.
Cast Edgar Markov the first turn you can pay six and take the heat that comes with him.
Say the eminence trigger out loud on every Vampire spell, including with Edgar in the command zone and never cast. Stack 010 proves the token is made and that Elspeth, Storm Slayer doubles it.
Commit a planeswalker only on a turn you can leave a blocker or a free answer up. Log 005: Elspeth came down, the attack went all-in on Tom, and she was taken down before the pings finished you.
alliances: Point Blood Artist's drain at the seat the table has already agreed to kill; Cruel Celebrant hits everyone and needs no such choice.

Ask the seat holding counterspells to cover the combo seat. You hold no stack interaction and five spot answers, so trade the jobs rather than duplicating them. Log 005 seated an Azorius counters deck at the same table as the deck that killed you.
Attack the seat that is winning and give the reason as board position. Log 004 removed Alex first on that ground and records it as position, not grudge.
Name the seat that has answered you twice and ask the table to split its answers. Log 002 lost to one seat picking off the card-flow permanents unopposed.
targets: Kill the seat that deals damage without attacking before the seat with the biggest board. In log 005 Tom's board was not the problem and Tom's pings closed the game.
Kill the seat that has stopped developing before the seat with the biggest board. In log 004 the seat holding no creatures is the seat that comboed out.

Aim removal at the permanent that answers you, not at the largest creature. Despark exiles a permanent at mana value four or greater for two mana, Anguished Unmaking exiles any nonland permanent for three mana and 3 life, Stroke of Midnight destroys a nonland permanent and hands back a 1/1.
Spend no answer on a land. Nothing in the 99 answers one, so a land-based lock is raced.
Deploy Cruel Celebrant ahead of Blood Artist when both are castable: each opponent against one target player.
